## Finding: a cost event was created 75 minutes after Pending Close

The relevant Racine manufacturing order is **MO-25-09-1070**, work-order ID **WO-2025-09-004**, for the **Cooler Plate Pack**. The supplied records show one cost event for this work order:

| Item | Recorded value |
|---|---|
| Source transaction | **TXN-ISSUE-250930-1070** |
| Cost-event ID | CE-250904-0004 |
| Event type | INPUT — component issue |
| Amount | **USD $284,763.42** (28,476,342 cents) |
| Event date | 2025-09-30 |
| Exact event-created time | **2025-09-30T19:15:00** |
| Exact September Pending Close time | **2025-09-30T18:00:00** |
| Time after Pending Close | **75 minutes — 1 hour 15 minutes** |
| Recorded accounting status | **POSTED** |

Calculation: `19:15:00 − 18:00:00 = 4,500 seconds ÷ 60 = 75 minutes`.

The timestamps above are reproduced exactly as recorded; the source does not specify a time zone.

## Policy assessment

**The recorded `POSTED` status is not consistent with Oracle’s documented Pending Close treatment for this newly created transaction.**

Oracle Fusion Cloud SCM Cost Management 26B states that new transactions falling in or before a Pending Close period are not staged in Cost Accounting or Receipt Accounting and are processed after the period is closed or reopened. Transactions created before Pending Close can continue processing. Revenue lines, COGS recognition, and manual cost adjustments are exceptions—but this event is an **INPUT/component issue**, not one of those exceptions.

**Sources:** `work_orders`, `cost_periods`, and `work_order_cost_events` in `system/oracle_scm_cost_management/state.db`; Oracle 26B documentation, “Cost Accounting Period Statuses and Transaction Accounting,” printed page **225** / PDF page **233**.

The review was read-only; no database records were changed. The audit result and provenance were saved to `/cache/work/worker_c837fabd75e2/audit-report.json`.
